# Conservative Party Manifesto 2024: Summary

## Economic Policy

The manifesto outlines plans to reduce National Insurance from 12% to 6% by April 2027, representing a £1,350 annual reduction for average workers. Self-employed individuals would see their main National Insurance rate abolished entirely. The party commits to maintaining fiscal rules requiring public sector debt to fall and borrowing to remain below 3% of GDP.

Business support includes maintaining "full expensing" tax policies, keeping corporation tax unchanged, and providing £4.3 billion in business rates support over five years. The VAT registration threshold has been raised to £90,000.

## Immigration and Borders

The manifesto proposes a legal cap on migration with annual parliamentary votes, continuing deportation flights to Rwanda, and reforming asylum rules through international cooperation. Visa fees would increase, and health checks would be required for migrants before travel.

## Public Services

NHS spending would increase above inflation annually, with plans to recruit 92,000 additional nurses and 28,000 doctors. The party proposes 250 new or modernised GP surgeries, 50 Community Diagnostic Centres, and expanded pharmacy services.

## Housing

A target of 1.6 million homes in England is proposed, with permanent Stamp Duty abolition for first-time buyers on properties up to £425,000 and a new Help to Buy scheme. Leasehold reform would cap ground rents at £250.

## Energy and Environment

The manifesto commits to net zero by 2050 while maintaining annual North Sea oil and gas licensing. Plans include tripling offshore wind capacity, building Small Modular Reactors, and investing in carbon capture technology.

## Defence and Security

Defence spending would increase to 2.5% of GDP by 2030, with continued support for Ukraine. The party proposes 8,000 additional police officers and mandatory National Service for 18-year-olds, offering either military or civic service options.

## Education

Proposals include the Advanced British Standard for 16-19 education, 100,000 additional apprenticeships, and mandatory mobile phone bans in schools.
